subject: Real-time API: degraded streaming throughput — immediate mitigation & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reyes <alex@novacommerce.com>, Priya Shah <priya@novacommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Real-time API: degraded streaming throughput — immediate mitigation & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

I’m writing to let you know we’re seeing elevated tail latency on our streaming/chat endpoints that’s impacting token delivery for some interactive sessions. We detected the issue at ~08:45 PST and are treating this as a high-severity incident.

What we know so far:
- Impact: delayed token emission (pause/stutter) for a subset of sessions in US-West; client-side connections remain open, but tokens arrive late or in bursts.
- Scope: preliminary signal indicates ~2–5% of your user sessions experienced visible degradation; engineering is validating counts now.

Immediate mitigations we’re applying (now):
1) Temporarily route affected sessions to a non-streaming endpoint (short-poll fallback) where token delivery is batched every 500ms.
2) Roll a compatible smaller model variant on overflow pool to reduce per-token compute and drop queuing pressure.
3) Increase shard capacity in US-West by provisioning two additional inference nodes.

We recommend the following client-side fallbacks while we stabilize (short checklist):
- If you rely on streaming SDKs, enable poll fallback (poll_interval=500ms) and implement a 3s stream_timeout before switching to poll.
- Add a retry with exponential backoff for partial-stream failures (start at 300ms).

I’ve attached an initial incident timeline and a short snippet you can use to enable poll fallback in your integration. We’ll follow up with a more detailed status update in ~30 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know interactive responsiveness is critical for NovaCommerce’s support flows.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-incident-timeline-20280303.pdf; streaming-fallback-snippet.txt

Is there an ETA on when you expect normal streaming behavior to resume? Also please confirm if the poll fallback preserves message ordering (we can tolerate sub-second grouping but not re-ordering).

Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 09:35:40 -07:00
Subject: RE: Real-time API: degraded streaming throughput — immediate mitigation & next steps

Kim / team — status from SRE/infra:

Preliminary root cause (in-flight): a KV-cache invalidation cascade on a subset of US-West shards caused synchronous cache warmups and a serialization point inside the streaming flush loop. That created bursts of CPU contention and delayed the token flush to clients.

Actions taken (09:20–09:32):
- Disabled prefix KV-cache for affected shards to avoid synchronous warmups.
- Scaled US-West shard pool by +2 nodes and pinned overflow traffic to a quantized model variant (q4_optimized) to reduce CPU pressure.
- Enabled short-term circuit-breaker on long-pending stream requests (requests > 6s) to surface retries earlier.

Observed effect: token emission delay metrics improving after 09:28; tail latency down ~65% on the impacted shards.

Next steps:
1) Collect debug traces and logs (pushing tarball to shared drive).
2) Run a controlled rollback of the cache change if qps stabilizes.
3) Prepare post-incident RCA and a permanent fix for cache eviction logic.

I’ll attach the debug logs once uploaded. Please share any additional customer-side telemetry.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reyes <alex@novacommerce.com>, Priya Shah <priya@novacommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Real-time API: degraded streaming throughput — immediate mitigation & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — quick update: engineering applied the mitigations Ben listed and we’re seeing substantial improvement in token pacing in US-West as of 09:30–09:40 PST. You should notice far fewer stalls; several of your agent sessions report normal flow again.

A few practical notes for NovaCommerce engineers:
- Poll fallback preserves ordering — the service batches tokens server-side and emits them in original sequence; client-side you’ll receive grouped tokens but order is guaranteed.
- If you can, set stream_timeout=3000ms and enable poll fallback in the SDK. We’ve attached the snippet we mentioned (streaming-fallback-snippet.txt).

We’ll continue monitoring for the next 12 hours and prepare a full postmortem for your team by Monday. If you’d like immediate telemetry, we can open a shared support ticket and push logs/trace IDs.

We also plan to offer a service credit for the disruption; we’ll confirm details in the postmortem.

Again, really sorry about the impact. Please let me know if you still see issues.

Thanks —
Kim

Subject: NV-20280303 — Post-incident summary and next steps (streaming latency)

Alex / Priya — attaching the post-incident summary and planned fixes (attached and linked). Key points below:

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-03-03 08:45–09:40 PST.
- Root cause: a cascade of KV-cache invalidations on US-West streaming shards that created synchronous cache warmups and a streaming flush serialization point under specific request patterns.
- Impact: elevated tail latency for ~2–5% of sessions in US-West; peak customer-visible lag ~3–8s for some interactive flows.

Immediate remediation applied:
- Disabled prefix KV cache on affected shards (reduces synchronous warmups).
- Scaled US-West pool and routed overflow to q4_optimized variant.
- Enabled circuit-breaker on long-pending streams to trigger earlier retry behavior.

Planned permanent fixes (timeline):
1) Cache eviction rewrite (INF-9821) — target: 2 weeks for PR + canary deploy.
2) Streaming flush path instrumentation and alerting — target: 1 week.
3) SDK fallback improvements + sample shipped to customers — target: 1 week.

Customer compensation: we propose a pro-rated credit covering the affected usage window; draft credit calculation and request form is attached.

Attachments included: redwood-incident-timeline-20280303.pdf; kvcache-debug-logs-20280303.tar.gz.

We’ll keep the Jira updated (link below) and will ping you as we deploy the permanent fixes. If you’d like a short technical readout with our engineering leads, we can schedule a 30-minute session this week.

Again, apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience.

Best,
Kimberly Park
